a:r.a:t: Rift comes with two additional tools that help with development and debugging.

The first is rift-tui - an interactive terminal UI for managing imposters. You can see all your loaded imposters, browse their stubs, view predicate and response details, and even generate curl commands for testing. It's useful when debugging why a request isn't matching the stub you expect.
The second is rift-lint - a configuration linter. You point it at your imposter directory and it validates everything:
- Do you have a catch-all stub that's shadowing more specific ones?
- Are there port conflicts between imposters?
This catches configuration errors before they cause test failures. You can run it in CI/CD to prevent broken configs from being merged.
